images.caption: Figure 2:Overview of the three-stage training pipeline of Sage-A1.5. First, the model is trained on diverse domain data, including coding, long-context reasoning, deep research, scientific reasoning, and co-working, utilizing environment construction, trajectory selection, staged supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning to build multi-domain teachers. Then, these teachers undergo unified outcome-process post-training to produce the final unified model, which features an agent orchestration for collaborative task solving, iterative agentic verification for reasoning reliability, and local deployment for ensuring data privacy, access control, and offline support.

Figure 11:Long-horizon scientific reasoning and self-correction of Sage-A1.5 on a quantum optics task from CritPt (#19). Through hypothesis formulation, tool-assisted verification, conflict detection, error localization and correction, Sage-A1.5 identifies and fixes an error in its numerical verification code, resolves discrepancies between its analytical derivation and numerical calculations, and independently re-validates the results.

Figure 15:Substituent effects and binding modes between N-methylacetamide (NMA) and pyridine derivatives in the Sage-A1.5 investigation.(a)Sage-A1.5 implemented and executed a scientist-guided computational workflow, managing independent jobs concurrently and diagnosing and restarting failed calculations.(b)Counterpoise-corrected gas-phase energy differences relative to NMA–pyridine; negative values indicate stronger binding. Each bar shows the lowest-energy sampled pose. The 2-methyl derivative binds more strongly than initially predicted.(c)Optimized NMA–3-hydroxypyridine complexes showing ring-nitrogen binding (N-HB, upper) and the more favorable hydroxyl binding (O-HB, lower). Dashed lines indicate hydrogen bonds. Atom colors: C (black), N (blue), O (red), H (white); carbon-bound hydrogens are omitted.
